root_idea.summary: The supplied evidence centers on the garment as a covering of the body: سِرْبَال denotes a shirt or garment, while related derived forms express putting on or becoming clothed in one.
root_idea.development: The lexical field extends from the garment noun to transitive and reflexive clothing constructions, a broader use for anything worn, protective mail or armor, and several specialized Classical extensions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the attested Classical singular citation form سِرْبَال rather than the Quranic plural morphology lemma سَرَٰبِيل.

senses.definition: A shirt or garment worn on the body.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic plural سَرَابِيل, this includes garments generally, including clothing associated with protection from heat.

senses.definition: A protective garment, specifically a coat of mail or armor used to guard against battle.
senses.usage_conditions: Attested in the Quranic plural سَرَابِيل for clothing that protects against the harm of combat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To clothe someone with a garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form I construction; the garment may be expressed directly or with بِـ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To clothe oneself or become clothed in a garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive or intransitive construction; the garment may be expressed directly or with بِـ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dish of broken or crumbled bread with grease, dripping, or gravy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized food term, distinct from the garment meanings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything worn as an article of dress or covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical nominal extension beyond the specifically attested Quranic applications; its plural is سَرَابِيل.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Metonymically, the office of the caliph.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use in which the garment metaphorically represents the office invested in its holder.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Transitive clothing use represented under the derived Classical verb.
Reflexive or self-clothing use represented under the derived Classical verb.
The unit supplies the shirt, coat-of-mail, and broader anything-worn branches; all are represented.

cautions: The Quranic evidence consists of the plural form سَرَابِيل; the public headword is normalized to the attested singular citation form سِرْبَال.
